name: GoFlow (Cloudflare)
what_it_is: GoFlow is a network flow collector written in Go that receives NetFlow v5, NetFlow v9, IPFIX, and sFlow v5 traffic, decodes it into protobuf messages, and publishes to Apache Kafka. It is the original Cloudflare implementation, now unmaintained in favor of the goflow2 fork.
components: Decoder — converts raw flow packet payloads into Go structs
Producer — protocol-specific transforms from decoded structs to protobuf messages
Transport — Kafka publisher (via Sarama) or console/stdout output
Monitoring — Prometheus metrics endpoint for decode time, sample rates, payload info, and NetFlow templates
protocols: IPFIX (with Option Data Sets for sampling rate and template management)
sFlow v5 (RAW, IPv4, IPv6, Ethernet, Gateway, router, and switch samples)
measurement: Prometheus metrics: decode time, sample rates, payload counters, NetFlow template tracking
40+ protobuf fields per flow record: src/dst IP, ports, AS numbers, VLAN IDs, TCP flags, ICMP type/code, MPLS labels, byte/packet counts
configuration: -nf.addr / -nf.port for NetFlow/IPFIX bind address and port
-sflow.addr / -sflow.port for sFlow bind address and port
-kafka.srv for DNS SRV-based Kafka broker discovery
-kafka=false to disable Kafka and fall back to console output
-workers to set number of worker goroutines
modes: Kafka mode (default): decode flows and publish protobuf to Kafka topics
Console mode (-kafka=false): decode flows and print to stdout
Debug mode: Docker image supports debug flag for verbose logging
constraints: Project is unmaintained; upstream recommends migrating to the goflow2 fork
No built-in flow storage or querying — requires external Kafka consumers for persistence
Template management for NetFlow v9/IPFIX is stateful; restarting the collector loses learned templates until re-advertised by exporters
No TLS support for Kafka connections documented in the original repo
docker_services: cloudflare/goflow:latest — main collector container (no docker-compose.yaml found in repository)
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yaml in the repository (404 on both master and main branches)
No fault injection or traffic simulation tooling
No built-in replay or pcap ingestion capability
No flow export back to network devices (receive-only)
